**Surah al-Ahqaf**

This surah is named (Surah al-Ahqaf) in all the copies of the Qur'an and the books of the Sunnah. This name is recorded in the words of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas. Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated with a good chain of transmission from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to me a surah from the *Ha Meems*, which is al-Ahqaf, and when a surah was more than thirty verses it was called "Thirty."

Likewise, its name is recorded in the words of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Al-Hakim narrated with a chain that he authenticated from Ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to me Surah al-Ahqaf... (the hadith).

The earlier hadith of Ibn 'Abbas implies that it is called "Thirty," but this does not belong exclusively to it, so it is not counted among its names. Al-Suyuti did not mention it in *al-Itqan* among the surahs that have more than one name.

The reason for its naming (al-Ahqaf) is the occurrence of the word *al-Ahqaf* in it, and it does not occur in any other surah of the Qur'an.

It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: by the consensus of all of them, and in the general statements of many exegetes. Some exegetes attributed the exception of some of its verses to some of those who hold that view. Ibn 'Atiyyah related the exception of two verses, which are His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 10] up to "the wrongdoers," for it refers to the conversion to Islam of 'Abdullah ibn Salam, and he embraced Islam only after the Hijrah; and His saying: ﴿So be patient as the steadfast messengers were patient﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35]. In *al-Itqan* there are three views on excepting three verses from it: the two that Ibn 'Atiyyah mentioned, and the third being ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15] up to His saying "losers." What follows will indicate that it was revealed after two years had passed since the beginning of the Prophethood,

[Page 6]

and the chains of transmission for all of them vary. The strongest of them is what was narrated concerning the first verse among them, and we will clarify that when discussing it in its places.

This surah is counted as the sixty-fifth in the order of revelation of the surahs. It was revealed after al-Jathiyah and before al-Dhariyat.

Its verses are counted by the majority of the scholars of the regions as thirty-four, and the people of Kufa counted them as thirty-five. The difference in that is based on whether *Ha Meem* is considered a separate verse or not.

**Its aims (aghrad)**

Among the aims that it contains: it opens, like surah al-Jathiyah, with what points to the inimitability of the Qur'an, as evidence that it is sent down from Allah.

Reasoning from the perfection of the creation of the heavens and the earth to the exclusive divinity of Allah, and to the establishment of the recompense for deeds.

Pointing to the occurrence of recompense after resurrection, and that this world is heading toward annihilation.

Refuting partners in divinity, and demonstrating that they are devoid of the attributes of divinity.

Refuting the claim that the Qur'an is the product of other than Allah.

Establishing the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and Allah's testimony to the truth of his prophethood, and the testimony of a witness of the Children of Israel, who is 'Abdullah ibn Salam.

Praise of those who believed in the Qur'an, and mention of some of their praiseworthy qualities, and what opposes them among the qualities of the disbelievers, and their envy which drove them to deny it.

It mentions the miracle of the jinn believing in the Qur'an.

The surah concludes with the affirmation of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Included in this is the treatment of parents and offspring, which is part of the character of the believers, and what is part of the character of the people of misguidance.

[Page 7]

And the lesson drawn from their misguidance despite the strength they possessed, and that Allah seized them for their disbelief, and destroyed other nations, making them a warning for the deniers, and that none of them were benefited by their fabricated lords.

It resembles many of the aims of surah al-Jathiyah, with variation.
